title: Test-time compute on a 0.06M-param weight-tied loop: trained at a FIXED K=3 the loop degrades past its trained depth (frontier acc 1.00 -> 0.55, easy instances 1.00 -> 0.71); trained with a STOCHASTIC depth schedule the identical model extrapolates to 2.67x the trained depth (0.85 at K=8, 11x full-sequence exact match)
hypothesis: A weight-tied looped block trained at K=3 loop iterations on a task whose difficulty is exactly the number of required sequential steps (prefix-parity under a 2-token attention window, where difficulty d needs K >= d-1) learns a REUSABLE one-step propagation rule, so running K > 3 at test time monotonically raises accuracy on harder instances instead of degrading it - and an untied depth-3 baseline with 2.6x the parameters cannot extend at all.
question: Does a weight-tied loop actually trade TEST-TIME compute for accuracy - i.e. does running more loop iterations at inference than at training improve accuracy on harder (deeper) instances - or does it degrade past K_train, which is the common failure? And if the axis exists at all, what decides which of the two you get?
method: The task is engineered so that test-time compute is the ONLY currency that buys accuracy. Prefix-parity (cumulative XOR): input [BOS, x_1..x_L] with x_i in {0,1}, target y_i = XOR(x_1..x_i). Attention is banded causal with WINDOW 1 - every position attends only to itself and its immediate predecessor - so after K applications of the block position i can only have seen bits [i-K, i], and difficulty d (= position index) is solvable IFF K >= d-1. There is no shallow heuristic and no parameter count that substitutes for a loop iteration; an ideal extrapolator sits at 1.00 on the analytically known frontier d = K+1 for every K, and a model that cannot reuse its own rule sits at chance 0.50 the moment d > K_train+1. Architecture: pre-LN transformer block, d_model 64, 2 heads, d_ff 256, NoPE (BOS token + the band supply all positional structure), final LayerNorm + 2-way linear readout; 58,370 params tied (50,178 without the injection adapter), 149,634 params for the untied depth-3 control (2.6x). Train: K=3, L ~ U{1..4} (exactly what 3 loops covers), AdamW lr 2e-3 wd 0.01, batch 256, 1500 steps, grad-clip 1.0, 100-step warmup. Test: K in {1..8} on 1024 held-out length-9 sequences at a fixed eval seed; because attention is causal, per-position accuracy on ONE length-9 batch yields every difficulty d=1..9 at once, giving a full accuracy(test K, difficulty) matrix. Four arms x 3 seeds = 12 runs: (1) tied_fixK3_inj - the backlog's literal spec, tied block at fixed K=3 with recurrent-depth-style per-iteration input injection (adapter on [h ; e]); (2) tied_fixK3_noinj - vanilla loop, no injection, the variant 2026-07-25_shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop flagged as its caveat; (3) tied_randK_inj - identical to (1) but trained with a STOCHASTIC depth schedule, k ~ U{1,2,3} per batch with L = k+1 so every supervised position is computable at the sampled depth (still never sees K>3 or L>4); (4) untied_d3 - 3 independent blocks evaluated once, plus two ad-hoc extensions it has no right to (repeat-last-block, cycle-blocks 0,1,2,0,1,2). Headline metric is FRONTIER ACCURACY = acc[K][d=K+1], the accuracy at the deepest difficulty K iterations could possibly solve, scored against ground truth rather than against another model.
architecture: weight-tied pre-LN transformer block, banded causal attention (window 1), NoPE, d_model 64 / 2 heads / d_ff 256, 58,370 params tied (50,178 no-injection) vs 149,634 untied depth-3

dataset.name: synthetic prefix-parity (cumulative XOR): [BOS, x_1..x_L] -> y_i = XOR(x_1..x_i); train L ~ U{1..4}, test L = 9 (1024 sequences, fixed eval seed 12345)
dataset.source: generated in run.py from the seed (torch.Generator, no external data)

task: prefix-parity / cumulative XOR with difficulty = required number of sequential propagation steps
compute: CPU single-threaded (torch.set_num_threads(1), OMP_NUM_THREADS=1), 638.8s wall clock for all 12 runs (4 arms x 3 seeds) incl. evaluation and chart, against a ~720s box

metrics.solvability_rule: difficulty d is solvable iff K >= d-1 (attention window 1)

untied_ad_hoc_extension_null.note: cycling blocks 0,1,2,0,1,2 leaves rows K=4 and K=5 bit-identical to K=3, then degrades

metrics.headline: The hypothesis as stated is REFUTED and the repair is decisive. Frontier accuracy (accuracy at difficulty d = K+1, the deepest instance K loops could possibly solve; chance 0.50, ideal 1.00): the backlog's literal arm tied_fixK3_inj runs 0.67 / 0.71 / 1.00 / 0.66 / 0.64 / 0.59 / 0.59 / 0.55 over K = 1..8 - perfect at the trained depth, then monotone DECAY, and the damage is not confined to hard instances: mean accuracy on the easy trained-depth difficulties (d <= 4) falls 1.000 -> 0.713 simply by running 8 loops instead of 3. Zero of 5 hard difficulties are monotone in K. The identical architecture and parameter count trained with a STOCHASTIC depth schedule (k ~ U{1,2,3}, L = k+1; still never sees K>3 or L>4) runs 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.96 / 0.95 / 0.89 / 0.87 / 0.85 - it tracks the ideal frontier out to K=8, 2.67x its trained depth, at a difficulty where every other arm is at chance. Full-sequence exact match on all 9 positions (requires 8 correct sequential steps) goes 0.038 at K=3 -> 0.428 at K=8, an 11x gain purely from test-time compute, vs 0.056 / 0.080 / 0.026 for the other three arms. All 3 seeds separate cleanly (0.77/0.83/0.95 vs 0.47/0.51/0.67). The untied depth-3 control with 2.6x the params matches every tied arm in-distribution (1.00 on d<=4 at K=3) and is at chance for every d>4 at every K; two ad-hoc extensions are exactly null (cycling leaves K=4 and K=5 bit-identical to K=3). Mechanism note: the failure is computational drift, not numerical blow-up - tied_fixK3_inj's residual norm is BOUNDED (9.4 -> 8.7 over 8 iterations) while it collapses, and tied_fixK3_noinj blows up 6.6x (13.7 -> 90.7) while staying the second most stable arm, because without input injection the loop converges to a FIXED POINT (rows K=4..8 nearly identical) - safe because it computes nothing new, and it never solves a single difficulty beyond d=4.

result_summary: The direct test of the 'test-time-compute axis' that 2026-07-25_shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop said the loop must earn its place on. Task built so the axis exists at all: prefix-parity with a WINDOW-1 banded causal attention, which makes difficulty d (= position index) solvable iff K >= d-1, so required sequential steps EQUAL difficulty and the ideal frontier d = K+1 is known analytically. 58k-param tied block, 3 seeds, 4 arms, 617s of one CPU thread. Every arm converges (train loss <= 5e-5) and every arm is perfect in-distribution (1.00 on d<=4 at K=3), so in-distribution fit is nowhere a confound. (1) THE BACKLOG'S LITERAL SETUP FAILS IN THE PREDICTED WAY. Trained at a fixed K=3, frontier accuracy is 1.00 at the trained depth and then decays to 0.55 at K=8; extra loops also corrupt instances the model had ALREADY solved, with mean accuracy on d<=4 falling 1.000 -> 0.713. None of the 5 hard difficulties is monotone in K. On this model, running more loops than you trained is strictly worse than stopping. (2) A STOCHASTIC DEPTH SCHEDULE FLIPS IT COMPLETELY. Same architecture, same 58,370 params, same 1500 steps, and still never more than 3 loops or 4 tokens in training - but sampling k ~ U{1,2,3} with L = k+1 yields 1.00/1.00/1.00/0.96/0.95/0.89/0.87/0.85 across K=1..8, i.e. real extrapolation to 2.67x the trained depth. Per difficulty, accuracy at the required K vs at K_train: d5 0.956 vs 0.503, d6 0.953 vs 0.509, d7 0.889 vs 0.503, d8 0.872 vs 0.497, d9 0.849 vs 0.505. Full-sequence exact match on all 9 positions rises 0.038 -> 0.428 (11x) purely from test-time compute; the other arms manage 0.056 / 0.080 / 0.026. All three seeds of the stochastic arm extrapolate (0.77/0.83/0.95 at K=8) and all three of the fixed-K arm fail (0.47/0.51/0.67) - no overlap. (3) THE UNTIED CONTROL CANNOT EXTEND AND NO HACK RESCUES IT. untied_d3 has 2.6x the parameters and ties every tied arm in-distribution, but its MAXIMUM accuracy anywhere in the entire d>4, K>3 region of the matrix is 0.511 - it never leaves chance, not once, in 40 cells. Repeating the last block gets d=5 to 0.501 at K=4; cycling blocks 0,1,2,0,1,2 leaves rows K=4 and K=5 bit-identical to K=3 and then degrades. Depth you did not tie is depth you cannot spend later. (4) THE FIXED-K FAILURE IS COMPUTATIONAL DRIFT, NOT NUMERICAL BLOW-UP. Residual-stream norm over 8 iterations: tied_fixK3_inj 9.4 -> 8.7 (bounded, and it collapses anyway) vs tied_fixK3_noinj 13.7 -> 90.7 (6.6x blow-up, and it is the SECOND MOST STABLE arm on easy instances, 1.000 -> 0.950). Norm growth and accuracy degradation are anti-correlated here. (5) INPUT INJECTION IS WHAT LETS A LOOP MOVE - AND THEREFORE BREAK. Without injection the loop converges to a fixed point (rows K=4..8 nearly identical, 1.00/1.00/0.91/0.91/0.65/...): extra loops are safe precisely because they compute nothing new, and it never solves a single difficulty beyond d=4. With injection the state keeps moving, which is the precondition both for extrapolation (arm 3) and for collapse (arm 1); the depth schedule alone decides which. IMPLICATION FOR SHADOW: this is the first axis on which the loop has earned anything, and it retro-explains three sibling nulls - shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop, shadow-recursion-capacity-window and shadow-halt-entropy-tiny ALL trained at fixed loop counts, which this run identifies as exactly the configuration in which the loop's one advantage does not exist. The ledger entry should read: tie the block, train the depth stochastically, or do not loop at all. It also explains why entropy halting was useless - an adaptive-depth policy needs a model whose quality varies usefully with depth, and a fixed-K-trained loop does not have one. CAVEATS, WORST FIRST. (a) THE TASK IS DESIGNED TO REWARD LOOPING: window-1 attention makes required steps exactly equal difficulty, the friendliest possible arena, and says nothing about whether natural-language difficulty has this structure (shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop suggests it does not). (b) One task, one architecture, one width, 3 seeds, 1500 steps. (c) The extrapolation is good but not perfect - 0.85 at K=8, decaying gently (0.96/0.95/0.89/0.87/0.85), so it presumably dies somewhere past K ~ 15; we did not find that point. (d) The stochastic arm differs from the fixed arm in TWO ways at once (random k AND the coupled L = k+1), so 'stochastic depth' here is the schedule as a package, not k-randomization alone. (e) Two metrics in results.json are brittle and are not the result: deepest_solved demands >= 95% on EVERY prefix, so a single 0.92 zeroes it and it badly under-reports the stochastic arm; and the strict 'nondecreasing' flag in monotonicity_by_arm fires false for the stochastic arm too, but only because of sub-1% jitter between chance-level cells (its d=5 runs 0.503 -> 0.509 -> 0.503 -> 0.956 over K=1..4). frontier_acc_by_arm is the metric to read. (f) Shrunk to a ~12-minute CPU box versus the backlog's ~1.5 hr estimate: 0.06M params, 1500 steps, lengths <= 9.

novelty_check.conclusion: Direct prior art exists and was read. arXiv:2606.29983 ('Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping') is the closest: on binary addition / Dyck-1 / Unique-Set / Copy with a looped 3-layer block trained on lengths < 20 and tested on lengths >= 20, it reports that fixed-loop-depth training produces runs with matched in-distribution accuracy but qualitatively different OOD behaviour (binary addition at fixed K=20: 34.2% OOD accuracy, std 7.4 across runs) and that SAMPLING THE LOOP COUNT during training substantially reduces that variance - the same mechanism our arm-1-vs-arm-3 contrast isolates, so the stochastic-depth fix is REPLICATED, not claimed as new. arXiv:2409.15647 (Looped Transformers for Length Generalization, UW-Madison, the backlog's listed prior art) establishes that looped transformers with an adaptive number of steps length-generalize on arithmetic and algorithmic tasks including parity. arXiv:2502.05171 (recurrent depth) is the source of the per-iteration input injection used here and of the test-time-compute framing, and also trains with a randomized recurrence count. WHAT THIS RUN ADDS: (i) SCALE - 58,370 parameters, 4 arms x 3 seeds, 617 s on ONE CPU thread, the cheapest demonstration of the effect we are aware of and cheap enough to serve as a regression test; (ii) the task is constructed so required sequential steps EQUAL the difficulty axis, which converts the usual single OOD-accuracy scalar into a 2-D accuracy(test K, difficulty) matrix with an analytically known ideal frontier d = K+1, so extrapolation is scored against ground truth rather than against another model; (iii) the untied-depth control is extended by two explicit hacks (repeat-last-block and cycle-blocks) and measured to be exactly null - prior art asserts untied depth cannot extend but does not quantify it; (iv) the norm-vs-accuracy DISSOCIATION - the arm whose residual norm blows up 6.6x is the stable one, while the norm-bounded arm is the one that collapses, and the no-injection loop is shown to be safe only because it converges to a fixed point - which we did not find reported; (v) direct linkage to the lab's own sibling nulls (shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop, shadow-recursion-capacity-window, shadow-halt-entropy-tiny), all of which trained at fixed loop counts.
